es: Separar lo comprobado de lo inferido y de lo que solo se cuenta en un texto que usa apparently, evidently, seems to have y it appears that.

teaching.en: Evidently, the window was broken from outside: the glass is all over the floor inside.
teaching.es: A todas luces, la ventana se rompió desde fuera: el cristal está por todo el suelo de dentro.
teaching.explanationEs: Evidently se apoya en algo que se ve: es una prueba directa.
segments: Evidently, the window was broken from outside: the
glass is all over the floor inside.
teaching.audioText: Evidently, the window was broken from outside: the glass is all over the floor inside.

teaching.en: It appears that the ball came through the window; the glass is our first clue.
teaching.es: Parece que la pelota entró por la ventana; el cristal es nuestra primera pista.
teaching.explanationEs: It appears that + oración marca una inferencia a partir de pistas, no una prueba directa.
segments: It appears that the ball came through the
window; the glass is our first clue.
teaching.audioText: It appears that the ball came through the window; the glass is our first clue.

teaching.en: The ball seems to have hit the window at high speed, but the witness did not see it.
teaching.es: La pelota parece haber golpeado la ventana a gran velocidad, pero la testigo no lo vio.
teaching.explanationEs: Seems to have + participio es una inferencia sobre el pasado, basada en lo que se observa.
segments: The ball seems to have hit the window at
high speed, but the witness did not see it.
teaching.audioText: The ball seems to have hit the window at high speed, but the witness did not see it.

teaching.en: Apparently, a witness saw two boys running away, but nobody has spoken to her yet.
teaching.es: Al parecer, una testigo vio a dos chicos huir corriendo, pero nadie ha hablado con ella todavía.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently suele marcar información de segunda mano: se oyó o se leyó, pero no se comprobó.
segments: Apparently, a witness saw two boys running away,
but nobody has spoken to her yet.
teaching.audioText: Apparently, a witness saw two boys running away, but nobody has spoken to her yet.

teaching.en: The football is our only clue, so the main suspect is a player.
teaching.es: El balón es nuestra única pista, así que el principal sospechoso es un jugador.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pista permite deducir, pero la deducción puede equivocarse.
segments: The football is our only clue, so
the main suspect is a player.
teaching.audioText: The football is our only clue, so the main suspect is a player.

teaching.en: There is a rumour that the manager broke it himself, but there is no evidence.
teaching.es: Corre el rumor de que el director la rompió él mismo, pero no hay pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Rumour = lo que circula sin pruebas; hay que separarlo de lo comprobado.
segments: There is a rumour that the manager broke
it himself, but there is no evidence.
teaching.audioText: There is a rumour that the manager broke it himself, but there is no evidence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tipo de información marca evidently en esta frase?

choices.text: Something the speaker heard from others.
Something the speaker guessed without clues.

feedback.es: Evidently se apoya en algo visible: aquí, el viento que entra por la habitación.

hint.es: Fíjate en qué dato de la frase se puede comprobar con los ojos.

origin.text: Evidently, the door was open: the wind was blowing through the room.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parece que la pelota rompió la ventana.»

feedback.es: Seems to have + participio expresa una inferencia sobre el pasado.

hint.es: Falta la palabra que une seems con have.

origin.text: The ball seems ___ have broken the window.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase marca información de segunda mano?

choices.text: Evidently, the teacher saw two boys.
Apparently, the teacher saw two boys.
The teacher seems to see two boys.

feedback.es: Apparently indica que lo cuenta otra persona y no se ha comprobado; evidently se apoya en algo que se ve.

hint.es: Busca el marcador de lo que alguien cuenta, no de lo que ves.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige en qué se basa la conclusión del hablante.

choices.text: On a witness who saw the thief.
On a video from a camera.
On the mud and the broken window he can see.

feedback.es: It appears that introduce una inferencia: se apoya en las pistas visibles, el cristal roto y el barro.

origin.audio: It appears that someone came in through the back door. The window is broken, and there is mud on the floor.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el tipo de información.

pairs: The thief seems to have used a key.
Apparently, the neighbour heard a noise.

feedback.es: Evidently es prueba directa, seems to have es inferencia y apparently marca lo que alguien cuenta.

pairs: The thief seems to have used a key.
Apparently, the neighbour heard a noise.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que alguien entró por la puerta trasera.»

answer.text: It appears that someone came in through the back door

feedback.es: It appears that + oración presenta una inferencia a partir de pistas.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué es información de segunda mano?

choices.text: A neighbour saw a red van nearby.
The lock is on the ground.

feedback.es: Apparently marca lo que cuenta la vecina sin confirmar; el candado en el suelo es visible y lo de las herramientas es una inferencia.

origin.text: Evidently, the shed was broken into: the lock is on the ground. It appears that the thief took only tools. Apparently, a neighbour saw a red van nearby, although nobody has confirmed it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la clase de información que contiene.

pairs: Evidently, the gate is wide open.
It appears that the thief knew the garden.
Apparently, the owner was away last week.

pairs.es: información de segunda mano: se cuenta

feedback.es: Cada marcador sitúa la información en un tipo distinto: prueba visible, deducción o rumor.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué es una inferencia del hablante.

feedback.es: Seems to have happened es una deducción (la tierra está mojada). Las huellas son prueba directa y lo del ruido es de segunda mano.

origin.audio: Evidently, someone was here: there are footprints near the gate. It seems to have happened at night, because the soil is still wet. Apparently, the neighbour heard a noise, but she is not sure.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El balón parece haber roto el cristal.»

answer.text: The ball seems to have broken the glass

feedback.es: La deducción sobre un hecho pasado se construye con seems + to have + participio, sin certeza absoluta.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que se distancia de la acusación.

feedback.es: Allegedly mantiene la distancia: alguien acusa, pero no hay pruebas. Evidently y undoubtedly afirman el hecho.

origin.text: Un periódico dice, sin pruebas, que el alcalde recibió regalos.

prompt.es: Completa: «El ruido lo hizo, en teoría, un gato, pero lo dudo.»

feedback.es: Conceivably expresa algo imaginable pero poco creíble.

origin.text: The noise was ___ made by a cat, but I doubt it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Con toda probabilidad, el ladrón volverá mañana.»

answer.text: In all likelihood the thief will come back tomorrow

feedback.es: In all likelihood expresa una hipótesis muy probable.
